title: NEB Class 11 Biology — Introduction To Biology — 2025
origin: curated NEB-pattern set covering every topic of the class-11 introduction to biology unit

questions.question: Define biology. Name its major branches and state the fields studied under pure and applied biology.
questions.solution:
Biology is the science of living things — their structure, function, growth, origin, evolution, distribution and classification.
Major branches: morphology, anatomy, physiology, cytology, genetics, evolution, taxonomy and ecology, split by group into botany, zoology and microbiology.
Pure biology studies life for knowledge — taxonomy, genetics, evolution, physiology — while applied biology uses that knowledge for practical ends: medicine, agriculture, animal husbandry, forestry, fisheries, biotechnology, pharmacy and environmental management.

questions.question: Explain the relationship of biology with chemistry, physics, mathematics and geography, giving one example each.
questions.solution:
Chemistry: explains the molecules of life — the structure of DNA and the action of enzymes are chemistry applied to living systems, and biochemistry grew from this link.
Physics: explains how organisms work — osmosis and diffusion, the optics of the eye, the mechanics of muscle and bone, the electricity of nerve impulses.
Mathematics: turns observations into testable models — Mendelian ratios, population growth equations, statistics used to test whether results are significant.
Geography and geology: explain where organisms live — climate, soil and landforms decide vegetation, and fossils in rock strata document evolution.

questions.question: What is the scientific method, and why is a control group necessary in an experiment?
questions.solution:
The scientific method is an orderly way of gaining reliable knowledge: observation, a question, a hypothesis, a controlled experiment, collection and analysis of data, and a conclusion that may support or reject the hypothesis, after which results are reported so others can repeat them.
A control group is treated exactly like the experimental group except for the one variable being tested. It shows what would have happened without the treatment, so any difference can be credited to that variable rather than to temperature, age or chance.

questions.question: Why is the study of biology important for Nepal? Give four points.
questions.solution:
1. Agriculture: most Nepalis depend on farming, so knowledge of crops, soil, pests, seeds and animal husbandry raises production and food security.
2. Health: understanding pathogens, immunity and nutrition supports disease control, vaccination and public-health planning in remote districts.
3. Natural resource management: forests, medicinal plants, biodiversity and watersheds need biological survey and conservation planning; biology also underlies ecotourism.
4. Biotechnology and environment: tissue culture, biofertilisers, biogas and bioremediation open new employment and help control pollution, while biology teaches how to protect the Himalayan ecosystems on which the country's water and climate depend.
